*University of Michigan* (1855) by [Jasper Francis Cropsey](/wiki/Jasper_Francis_Cropsey "Jasper Francis Cropsey")

[Henry Philip Tappan](/wiki/Henry_Philip_Tappan "Henry Philip Tappan") became the university's first president in 1852, with the ambition to shape the institution as a model for future universities. During his decade of service, he overhauled the curriculum,[[65]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194239–53-69) expanded the library and museum collections,[[65]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194239–53-69) established the law school, and supervised the construction of the [Detroit Observatory](/wiki/Detroit_Observatory "Detroit Observatory").[[65]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194239–53-69) He secularized faculty appointments by prioritizing merit in selections,[[65]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194239–53-69) breaking away from the retrograde tradition of regents distributing positions among Protestant denominations.[[65]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEShaw194239–53-69) In 1855, Michigan became the second university in the country to issue [Bachelor of Science](/wiki/Bachelor_of_Science "Bachelor of Science") degrees.[[66]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHinsdale190648-70) The following year, the country's first chemical laboratory was built on campus, specifically designed for chemistry education, providing additional space for classes and laboratories. Further information: [Franco-Spanish War (1635–1659)](/wiki/Franco-Spanish_War_(1635%E2%80%931659) "Franco-Spanish War (1635–1659)")

Sensing imminent death in the spring of 1643, King [Louis XIII](/wiki/Louis_XIII "Louis XIII") decided to put his affairs in order for his four-year-old son Louis XIV. Not trusting the judgement of his Spanish wife Queen Anne, who would normally have become the sole [regent](/wiki/Regent "Regent") of France, the king decreed that a regency council would rule on his son's behalf, with Anne at its head.[[10]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEReinhardt201620-12)

Louis XIII died on 14 May 1643. On 18 May[[11]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKleinman1985145-13) Queen Anne had her husband's will annulled by the *[Parlement](/wiki/Parlement "Parlement")* of Paris, a judicial body of nobles and high-ranking clergy,[[12]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBély200157-14) and she became sole regent. She exiled her husband's ministers Chavigny and Bouthilier and appointed the [Count of Brienne](/wiki/Henri-Auguste_de_Lom%C3%A9nie,_comte_de_Brienne "Henri-Auguste de Loménie, comte de Brienne") as her minister of foreign affairs.[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTESonnino1998217–218-15) Anne kept the direction of religious policy strongly in hand until her son's majority in 1661.

She appointed [Cardinal Mazarin](/wiki/Cardinal_Mazarin "Cardinal Mazarin") as chief minister, giving him the daily administration of policy. She continued the policies of her late husband and [Cardinal Richelieu](/wiki/Cardinal_Richelieu "Cardinal Richelieu"), despite their persecution of her, in order to win absolute authority in France and victory abroad for her son. Anne protected Mazarin by exiling her followers the [Duke of Beaufort](/wiki/C%C3%A9sar_de_Bourbon "César de Bourbon") and [Marie de Rohan](/wiki/Marie_de_Rohan "Marie de Rohan"), who conspired against him in 1643.[[14]](#cite_note-16)

In 1965, ten-year-old Roberts and his family moved to [Long Beach, Indiana](/wiki/Long_Beach,_Indiana "Long Beach, Indiana"), where his father became the manager of a new steel plant in nearby [Burns Harbor](/wiki/Burns_Harbor,_Indiana "Burns Harbor, Indiana").[[15]](#cite_note-nytimes-15) By age 13, Roberts "already had a clear plan for his life."[[16]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStone20201015–1016-16) He attended the parochial [La Lumiere School](/wiki/La_Lumiere_School "La Lumiere School"),[[17]](#cite_note-:1-17) an academically rigorous [Catholic boarding school](/wiki/Catholic_school "Catholic school") in [La Porte, Indiana](/wiki/La_Porte,_Indiana "La Porte, Indiana"),[[18]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStone20201015-18) where he captained the school's [football](/wiki/American_football "American football") team, participated in track and field, and was a regional champ

fanoutqa_016238.t: Mark Zuckerberg :: Depictions in media :: The Social Network :: Disputed accuracy :: chunk_0016
fanoutqa_016238.x:
Mark Zuckerberg :: Depictions in media :: The Social Network :: Disputed accuracy :: chunk_0016
According to [David Kirkpatrick](/wiki/David_Kirkpatrick_(author) "David Kirkpatrick (author)"), former technology editor at *[Fortune](/wiki/Fortune_(magazine) "Fortune (magazine)")* magazine and author of *[The Facebook Effect: The Inside Story of the Company That Is Connecting the World](/wiki/The_Facebook_Effect "The Facebook Effect")* (2011),[[104]](#cite_note-105) "the film is only 40% true ... he is not snide and sarcastic in a cruel way, the way Zuckerberg is played in the movie." He says that "a lot of the factual incidents are accurate, but many are distorted, and the overall impression is false" and concludes that primarily "his motivations were to try and come up with a new way to share information on the Internet".[[105]](#cite_note-BBCmovie-106)

Although the film portrayed Zuckerberg's creation of Facebook in order to elevate his stature after not getting into any of the elite [final clubs](/wiki/Officially_unrecognized_Harvard_College_social_clubs "Officially unrecognized Harvard College social clubs") at Harvard, Zuckerberg stated that he had no interest in joining the clubs.[[7]](#cite_note-NEWYORKER2010-8) Kirkpatrick agreed that the impression implied by the film is "false". Karel Baloun, a former senior engineer at Facebook, noted that the "image of Zuckerberg as a socially inept nerd is overstated ... It is fiction ...". He likewise dismissed the film's assertion that he "would deliberately betray a friend".[[105]](#cite_note-BBCmovie-106)

fanoutqa_002158.t: Ovarian cancer :: Diagnosis :: Staging :: Grading :: chunk_0036
fanoutqa_002158.x:
Ovarian cancer :: Diagnosis :: Staging :: Grading :: chunk_0036
Grade 1 tumors have well-differentiated cells (look very similar to normal tissue) and are the ones with the best prognosis. Grade 2 tumors are also known as moderately well-differentiated, and they are composed of cells that resemble normal tissue. Grade 3 tumors have the worst prognosis, and their cells are abnormal, referred to as poorly differentiated.[[85]](#cite_note-85)

Metastasis in ovarian cancer is very common in the abdomen and occurs via exfoliation, where cancer cells burst through the ovarian capsule and can move freely throughout the peritoneal cavity. Ovarian cancer metastases usually grow on the surface of organs rather than the inside; they are also common on the omentum and the peritoneal lining. Cancer cells can also travel through the [lymphatic system](/wiki/Lymphatic_system "Lymphatic system") and metastasize to lymph nodes connected to the ovaries via blood vessels; i.e. the lymph nodes along the [infundibulopelvic ligament](/wiki/Suspensory_ligament_of_ovary "Suspensory ligament of ovary"), the [broad ligament](/wiki/Broad_ligament_of_the_uterus "Broad ligament of the uterus"), and the [round ligament](/wiki/Round_ligament_of_uterus "Round ligament of uterus"). The most commonly affected groups include the [paraaortic](/wiki/Paraaortic_lymph_node "Paraaortic lymph node"), [hypogastric](/w/index.php?title=Hypogastric_lymph_node&action=edit&redlink=1 "Hypogastric lymph node (page does not exist)"), [external iliac](/wiki/External_iliac_lymph_nodes "External iliac lymph nodes"), [obturator](/w/index.php?title=Obturator_lymph_nodes&action=edit&redlink=1 "Obturator lymph nodes (page does not exist)"), and [inguinal lymph nodes](/wiki/Inguinal_lymph_node "Inguinal lymph node"). Usually, ovarian cancer does not metastasize to the liver, lung, brain, or kidneys unless it is a recurrent disease; this differentiates ovarian cancer from many other forms of cancer.[[30]](#cite_note-Hoffman

Ivy League :: History of diversity :: Racial segregation and integration :: chunk_0016
Ivy League institutions have a complex history of racial segregation, and, eventually, integration. All of the universities in the Ivy League besides Cornell University were chartered during the [American era of slavery](/wiki/Slavery_in_the_United_States "Slavery in the United States").[[117]](#cite_note-Bradley-2021-122) In 2003, Brown University was the first of the Ivies to take accountability for their historic ties to slavery and the [transatlantic slave trade](/wiki/Atlantic_slave_trade#:~:text=The_Atlantic_slave_trade,_transatlantic,16th_to_the_19th_centuries. "Atlantic slave trade").[[118]](#cite_note-Brown's_Slavery_&_Justice_Report,_Digital_2nd_Edition_|_Brown_University-123)[[119]](#cite_note-124) Following Brown, other Ivy League universities formed committees to examine their ties to slavery, and found various institutional relationships to slavery. Yale University, for example, used profits from slave traders and owners to fund its first scholarships, libraries, and faculty positions.[[120]](#cite_note-125)[[121]](#cite_note-126) To date, some of Yale's residential colleges are named after slave traders and supporters.[[122]](#cite_note-127) The investigations at Harvard, Princeton, Columbia, and the University of Pennsylvania all found that, in the century following their charters, enslaved Black people lived on campus to care for students, professors, or the universities' presidents.[[123]](#cite_note-128)[[124]](#cite_note-slavery.princeton.edu-129)[[125]](#cite_note-Time-130)[[126]](#cite_note-131) Notably, Princeton's first nine presidents were slave owners, and in 1766, a slave auction reportedly took place on Princeton's campus.[[124]](#cite_note-slavery.princeton.edu-129)

fanoutqa_028014.x:
Drew Gilpin Faust :: Career :: part 03 :: chunk_0004
In 2016, Harvard began to study its own historical involvement with slavery. This occurred after Faust publicly acknowledged that the school had been "directly complicit in America's system of racial bondage". She oversaw the installation on campus of a commemorative plaque to honor the enslaved whose labor was exploited by the institution. Her successor, [Lawrence Bacow](/wiki/Lawrence_Bacow "Lawrence Bacow"), subsequently commissioned a formal study in 2019, continuing Faust's work.[[33]](#cite_note-33)

Faust retired as Harvard president in June 2018. Four days later, she joined the Board of Directors of [Goldman Sachs](/wiki/Goldman_Sachs "Goldman Sachs"). She retained her title as Professor of History at Harvard.[[34]](#cite_note-34)

In 2023, Faust published a memoir, *Necessary Trouble*, about growing up in a conservative family in segregated Virginia. It describes her awakening to the [Civil Rights movement](/wiki/Civil_Rights_movement "Civil Rights movement") that was occurring around her. For example, regarding the [national news story](/wiki/Little_Rock_Nine "Little Rock Nine") in 1957 about the attempted integration of [Little Rock Central High School](/wiki/Little_Rock_Central_High_School "Little Rock Central High School") in [Little Rock, Arkansas](/wiki/Little_Rock,_Arkansas "Little Rock, Arkansas"), she writes: "I was 9 years old when the news reports about "massive resistance" and battles over segregation made me suddenly realize that it was not a matter of accident that my school was all-white."[[35]](#cite_note-35)[[36]](#cite_note-36)[[37]](#cite_note-37)

Geography of Singapore :: Topography :: Land reclamation :: chunk_0002
Main article: [Land reclamation in Singapore](/wiki/Land_reclamation_in_Singapore "Land reclamation in Singapore")

Singapore has engaged in extensive [land reclamation](/wiki/Land_reclamation_in_Singapore "Land reclamation in Singapore") since the [British colonisation in 1819](/wiki/Founding_years_of_modern_Singapore "Founding years of modern Singapore"), using earth sourced from its own hills, the seabed and neighbouring countries.[[3]](#cite_note-3) As a result, the country's land area has expanded from approximately 582 square kilometres (225 sq mi) in the 1960s to around 745 square kilometres (288 sq mi) in the 2020s. Reclamation continues today with the use of newer methods such as [polders](/wiki/Polder "Polder") and [barrages](/wiki/Barrage_(dam) "Barrage (dam)") to counter rising sea levels.[[4]](#cite_note-4)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Juego_de_pelota_chichen_itza.jpg/250px-Juego_de_pelota_chichen_itza.jpg)](/wiki/File:Juego_de_pelota_chichen_itza.jpg)

The [Grand Ballcourt](/wiki/Mesoamerican_ballcourt "Mesoamerican ballcourt") structures

The layout of Chichen Itza site core developed during its earlier phase of occupation, between 750 and 900 AD.[[26]](#cite_note-CobosPalma0405p531-29) Its final layout was developed after 900 AD, and the 10th century saw the rise of the city as a regional capital controlling the area from central Yucatán to the north coast, with its power extending down the east and west coasts of the peninsula.[[27]](#cite_note-30) The earliest [hieroglyphic](/wiki/Maya_script "Maya script") date discovered at Chichen Itza is equivalent to 832 AD, while the last known date was recorded in the Osario temple in 998.[[28]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOsorio_León2006457-31)

**Telephone numbers in Pakistan** are ten digits long. Landline numbers and mobile numbers have different structures. Geographically fixed landline are prefixed by an area code which varies in length depending on the significance of the place. Mobile numbers are prefixed followed by a two-digit code indicating the telephone operator. The international country code for Pakistan is +92.
